newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies fall limit on cash concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies fall limit on cash concerns.

text.p: Reports that packers were willing to lower asking prices overnight for cash bellies sparked long liquidation that took CME pork bellies down the daily limit in nearbys, traders said. Hog futures also fell with deferreds down most on early projections for the Hog and Pigs report later in the month, sources said.

At 1116 CDT, pork bellies stood 3.000 to 2.500 cents per lb lower with July and August limit down, putting July at 87.250 cents. Hog futures fell 0.225 to 1.450 cents with June off the least at 81.000 cents. February paced the setback in deferred months.

Reports that packers reduced asking prices for cash bellies added to early long liquidation that knocked pork belly futures down the limit. Packers were asking up to $92 per cwt for cash bellies Wednesday with bids at $87 to $88 and offerings came down to $88 to $89 cents, cash sources said.

Belly futures tumbled early when unexpected long liquidation took traders by surprise. Futures appeared overbought but few traders expected the volume of selling that developed at the opening, traders said.
E.D.& F. Man and Lind-Waldock notably sold into sell stops. Locals bought near the low, pit sources said.

Hog futures also fell as profit taking weighed on nearbys, traders said. Packers were willing to raise bids to encourage increased hog movement, sources said. That movement pressured the market after lows were tested early and held, traders said.

New hedge selling and long liquidation touched off sell stops in deferreds. Selling appeared to be developing on early outlooks that the upcoming USDA Hog and Pigs report will show a substantial expansion of the breeding herd, they said.
Rand Financials generally sold July and August. Dean Witter and ING bought July early. In hog options, First Chicago bought July 78 and 80 puts, pit sources said.
